To ensure the system crashes when a deadlock is detected, we run all tests using custom builds.

> 4.6.3 (35e80b3a8822a9df9be390814b62f44c0a9c69e8): 

A freeze occurs in the same way, but the call stack looks different. There are multiple worker threads with deeply nested calls to `_wait_collaboratively`.

~~No freeze occurs.~~

After changing the number of cores in the Android emulator to 3, it started freezing. (I had been testing with 6 up until then.)
The call stack is the same as in 4.7.1.

> 4.8.dev1 (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/ebbf577a041d1ab8d7824b6f90e7d0575461ca45):

The caller thread can't call the function `get_script()` on this node. Use `call_deferred()` or `call_deferred_thread_group()` instead.

I might be missing some background here, but Godot's cooperative waiting — where wait_for_task_completion may run an arbitrary queued task via _wait_collaboratively — seems prone to causing a variety of subtle problems. And with WorkerThreadPool exposed to GDScript, careful engine-side programming alone can't prevent user code from hitting the same pitfalls.

A fundamental rework (e.g., C++20 coroutines) would be great, but until then, simpler options that err on the side of safety might also be worth considering — for example, an opt-in setting to grow the pool dynamically (with a hard cap and a saturation warning), which requires no cooperation from user code and leaves default behavior untouched. Just a suggestion.

FYI: #87990 (and I guess #88241)

I'm not sure if it's the exact same problem, but the callstacks look somewhat similar, so this might not be a regression in 4.7 at least, since that particular `lock-order-inversion` error has prevented `use_tsan=yes` from running cleanly for years at this point.
